title: Write error_code values in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE

facts.note: Test files are excluded (source exception S024); every non-test file is in scope.

Emitted by bun_security_hygiene_detector when an `"error_code": "<value>"` / `errorCode` value in a non-test file fails ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$; applies to existing and new code alike. Requires the detector output to be wired in as an activation observer.

fires: A non-test file contains an `error_code` value that is camelCase or lower-case (e.g. "orderNotFound"), whether newly written or already present.
A non-test file sets `errorCode` to a value that does not match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$.
A non-test file contains both `notFound` and `NOT_FOUND` style codes for one condition.
doesNotFire: A test file contains an error_code value in any case.
A human-readable message field (separate from error_code) contains mixed-case text.
Other string values that are not under the `error_code` / `errorCode` key.

given: A non-test file contains an `error_code` (or `errorCode`) key with a string value
when: that file is written, changed, or checked
then: The `error_code` / `errorCode` value MUST be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$`.
prefer: Put human-readable messages in a separate field, which is not constrained.
avoid: Writing `{ error_code: "orderNotFound" }` or any non-UPPER_SNAKE_CASE code.
Mixing spellings for one condition (`notFound` beside `NOT_FOUND`), which yields two codes for one condition.
unless: Only the `error_code` / `errorCode` key is checked; other string values, including human-readable messages in a separate field, are out of scope.
why: An error code is the machine key a client branches on, so once a client does, its spelling is API surface; an inconsistent set (`notFound` beside `NOT_FOUND`) produces two codes for one condition that no testing reconciles because both are 'working'. The case convention itself is arbitrary; that it is uniform is not.
evidence: bun_security_hygiene_detector reports no ERROR-CODE-FORMAT-001 finding on non-test files.
Every `error_code` / `errorCode` value in non-test files matches `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$`.
verifier_detail: Match `"error_code": "<value>"` and the `errorCode` spelling; test the value against `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$`.
Only the `error_code` / `errorCode` key is checked; other string values are out of scope; human-readable messages belong in a separate field and are not constrained.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

Stack-neutral obligation, and the second of only two rules in this family that PORTS verbatim: the payload is JSON, so the pattern and the case test carry over from the python-pytest sibling `coder.error-response.code-format` unchanged.
Realized by `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (implementation type validator), core alias ERROR-CODE-FORMAT-001; metadata.aliases ["ERROR-CODE-FORMAT-001"].

Terms: error_code — the machine key a client branches on; once it does, the spelling is API surface. upper_snake_case — `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$`; the convention itself is arbitrary; that it is uniform is not.
